questions.prompt: Normal take-off: what is the FIRST call-out, made after confirming the correct runway from signage/markings?
choices: “Approach sector and runway clear”
“Runway [number], identified”
“Runway heading verified”
“Airspeed alive”
questions.explanation: QRC Exercise 12, Normal take-off item 1: confirm correct runway from signage/markings and call “Runway [number], identified”. The other calls come later in the sequence.

questions.prompt: Which option lists only correct line-up items per the QRC?
choices: Parking brakes released; transponder ALT; landing light on when clearance received; pitot heat ON in visible moisture or OAT below +5°C
Parking brakes set; transponder ALT; landing light on when clearance received; pitot heat ON below +15°C
Parking brakes released; transponder 7700; landing light off for take-off; pitot heat ON in visible moisture or OAT below +5°C
Parking brakes released; transponder ALT; landing light on only after rotation; pitot heat ON below +10°C
questions.explanation: QRC Exercise 12, line-up items: parking brakes released; transponder ALT; landing light on when clearance received; pitot heat ON in visible moisture or if OAT is below +5°C.

questions.prompt: Per the line-up items, when must the pitot heat be switched ON?
choices: Only when flying in IMC
In visible moisture or if OAT is below +5°C
Whenever OAT is below +15°C
Only at night
questions.explanation: QRC Exercise 12, line-up items: “Pitot heat ON (in visible moisture or if OAT is below +5°C)”.

questions.prompt: What does the CED check consist of during the take-off roll, before calling “Take-off power set”?
choices: Power 100% / 2300 RPM / all indications green
Power 90% / 2100 RPM / all indications green
Power 100% / 2500 RPM / fuel flow stable
Power 65% / 2300 RPM / all indications green
questions.explanation: QRC Exercise 12, Normal take-off item 10: “Check CED — power 100% / 2300 RPM / all indications green”, call out “Take-off power set”.

questions.prompt: Normal take-off (DA40-TDI): give the QRC values for rotation, initial climb, flap retraction height and final climb speed.
questions.explanation: QRC Exercise 12, Normal take-off items 13, 14, 17, 18: rotate at 60 KIAS (Vr), climb 70 KIAS, flaps up passing 200 ft AGL, then climb 80 KIAS.

questions.prompt: Crosswind take-off in a strong crosswind (1/2 gust): what rotation speed does the QRC prescribe?
choices: Vr – 5 KIAS
Vr + max 5 KIAS
Vr + max 10 KIAS
Vr + max 15 KIAS
questions.explanation: QRC Exercise 12, Crosswind take-off item 2: “Vr + max 5 KIAS during strong crosswind (1/2 gust)”.

questions.prompt: Order the key steps of the short field take-off.
steps: Line up at the very beginning of the runway (use all available length)
Hold the brakes and set full power (100%) 2300 RPM
Check power / engine instruments
Release brakes, heels on the floor
Rotate at 55 KIAS (Vr)
Accelerate in ground effect once airborne
Start climb when speed > 59 KIAS
questions.explanation: QRC Exercise 12, Short field take-off: line up at the very beginning, hold brakes, full power 100%/2300 RPM, check instruments, release brakes, rotate 55 KIAS, accelerate in ground effect, climb when >59 KIAS.

questions.prompt: Soft field take-off: when do you release the back pressure on the stabilator?
choices: When the nose wheel lifts off
At 55 KIAS
Passing 200 ft AGL
When full power is set
questions.explanation: QRC Exercise 12, Soft field take-off: make a rolling take-off, maintain back pressure on the stabilator, and “release back pressure when nose wheel lifts off”.

questions.prompt: Obstacle take-off: what is the initial climb speed, and what speed is flown after passing the obstacle?
choices: 55 KIAS initial, 70 KIAS after the obstacle
60 KIAS initial, 70 KIAS after the obstacle
70 KIAS initial, 80 KIAS after the obstacle
59 KIAS initial, 80 KIAS after the obstacle
questions.explanation: QRC Exercise 12, Obstacle take-off: “Initial climb 59 KIAS; speed 80 KIAS after passing obstacle”.

questions.prompt: In the normal circuit, what speed and power setting are used after levelling off at circuit altitude?
choices: 110 KIAS, ±65% power
90 KIAS, ±45% power
80 KIAS, ±15% power
75 KIAS, power idle
questions.explanation: QRC Exercise 13, Normal circuit item 2: “Speed 90 KIAS, power ±45%”. (110/65% is cruise, 80/15% relates to base, 75 is glide.)

questions.prompt: Which bank limits apply in the normal circuit per the QRC?
choices: 20° for all turns in the circuit
30° bank for the crosswind and downwind turns; climbing turn after passing 200 ft max 20° bank; turn to final max 30° bank
45° bank for crosswind/downwind turns; 30° bank on final
30° bank for crosswind/downwind turns; climbing turn max 30°; final turn max 45°
questions.explanation: QRC Exercise 13, Normal circuit: turns to crosswind and downwind use 30° bank (items 3, 5); a climbing turn after passing 200 ft is permitted with max 20° bank (item 4); turn to final uses maximum 30° of bank (item 11). (45° bank is the steep turn in Exercise 15.)

questions.prompt: Recite the FRESBL downwind checks from memory, with the content of each item.
questions.model_answer: F — Flaps: check speed, call “SPEED CHECKED” → select flaps take-off. R — Radio: downwind call (e.g., PH-RAB downwind runway 06). E — Engine: instruments in green, fuel quantity & balance checked. S — Security: harnesses secure, loose items stowed. B — Brakes: check pressure, heels on floor. L — Lights: landing light ON.
questions.explanation: QRC Exercise 13, Normal circuit item 6 lists the FRESBL downwind checks exactly as in the model answer.

questions.prompt: Normal circuit, base to final: give the QRC power setting on base, the descent speed, and the final approach speed with flaps LDG.

parts.label: Maintain altitude until, then descend at

questions.explanation: QRC Exercise 13, Normal circuit items 8, 9, 12: reduce power to ±15% on base, maintain altitude until 80 KIAS then start descent, on final flaps LDG and 70 KIAS trimmed.

questions.prompt: Order the normal circuit flow from downwind to established final.
steps: Perform the downwind checks (FRESBL)
Turn to base leg when the runway is 45° behind
Reduce power to ±15%
Maintain altitude until 80 KIAS, then start the descent
Turn to final with maximum 30° of bank
On final: flaps LDG, 70 KIAS, trimmed
Establish on a stabilized glide path
questions.explanation: QRC Exercise 13, Normal circuit items 6–13 in this order.

questions.prompt: Order the go-around steps.
steps: Call: “Going-around!”
Set full power (100%)
Pitch up to arrest the descent (look outside)
Set flaps take-off
Pitch for climb attitude (70 KIAS)
Maintain coordinated flight and reset trim
questions.explanation: QRC Exercise 13, Go-around items 1–7: call “Going-around!”, full power 100%, pitch up to arrest descent, flaps T/O, climb at 70 KIAS, stay coordinated, reset trim.

questions.prompt: Crosswind landing: how is the aircraft aligned with the centreline just before touchdown?
choices: Keep the crab angle through touchdown
Bank away from the wind and use aileron to align
Use rudder to de-crab and line up, while banking into the wind
Touch down on the nose wheel first, then align
questions.explanation: QRC Exercise 13, Crosswind landing items 4–5: use rudder to de-crab and line up with the centreline, at the same time bank into the wind to stay above the centreline; land on the main wheels.

questions.prompt: Short field landing: what is the approach speed, and how is the power closed?
choices: 65 KIAS; close the power lever gently in the tempo of the flare, ideally just closed at touchdown
70 KIAS; close the power fully abeam the threshold
75 KIAS; keep power on until after touchdown
60 KIAS; close the power at the start of final
questions.explanation: QRC Exercise 13, Short field landing: power/attitude 65 KIAS, close the power lever gently in the tempo of the flare; ideally power should just be closed as the aircraft touches down (not before!).

questions.prompt: Touch and go: after aiming for the centreline, what is the correct sequence of configuration and power?
choices: Flaps LDG, power ±45%
Flaps up, full power 100%/2300 RPM
Set flaps take-off (visual check), full power 100%/2300 RPM
Keep flaps landing, full power 100%/2300 RPM
questions.explanation: QRC Exercise 13, Touch and go: aim for the centreline, set flaps take-off (visual check), full power 100%/2300 RPM, proceed as normal take-off.

questions.prompt: Normal landing: which description matches the QRC?
choices: Aim for the aiming point, keep ±15% power through touchdown, touch down on the nose wheel first, do the after landing checks on downwind
Close the power at the start of final, hold 75 KIAS to touchdown, touch down on all wheels at once, do the after landing checks before vacating
Aim for the aiming point, close the power lever gently, flare, touch down on the main wheels, and perform the after landing checks after passing the stop bar
Aim at 1/3 of the runway, keep 70 KIAS to the flare, touch down tail-low on grass only, do the after landing checks on the runway
questions.explanation: QRC Exercise 13, Normal landing: aim for the aiming point, close the power lever gently, flare (item 10), touchdown on main wheels (item 11); after landing checks are memory items performed after passing the stop bar (item 16). (75 KIAS is the glide speed; aiming at 1/3 of the field belongs to the forced landing, Exercise 16.)

questions.prompt: Steep turn entry: what speed and bank angle does the QRC prescribe?
choices: 110 KIAS, 45° bank
90 KIAS, 30° bank
110 KIAS, 30° bank
80 KIAS, 45° bank
questions.explanation: QRC Exercise 15, Steep turn: speed 110 KIAS, roll into 45° bank using rudder to counteract adverse yaw.

questions.prompt: During the steep turn, how is power managed?
choices: Increase power by ±10% passing 30° bank; reduce power by ±10% when passing 30° bank on roll-out
Full power at 45° bank; idle on roll-out
Reduce power by ±20% passing 30° bank; increase on roll-out
Power is kept at ±65% throughout
questions.explanation: QRC Exercise 15, Steep turn items 4 and 7: passing 30° bank increase power by ±10%; when passing 30° of bank on roll-out, reduce power by ±10%.

questions.prompt: Steep turn: give the QRC entry speed, bank angle, and the bank angle at which the power change is made.
questions.explanation: QRC Exercise 15, Steep turn: 110 KIAS, 45° bank, power ±10% passing 30° bank (both rolling in and rolling out).

questions.prompt: Order the steep turn steps.
steps: Look out – scan for traffic and select an outside reference point
Set speed 110 KIAS
Roll into 45° bank, using rudder to counteract adverse yaw
Passing 30° bank, increase power by ±10%
Check bank/slip indicator, altitude/pitch, and maintain 110 KIAS
Roll out using rudder; passing 30° bank reduce power by ±10%
Adjust pitch for horizontal flight
questions.explanation: QRC Exercise 15, Steep turn items 1–8 in this order.

questions.prompt: Order the spiral dive recovery steps.
steps: Reduce the power
Roll out gently, wings level
Pitch up gently to climb attitude
Apply full power when the nose passes the horizon
Climb back to desired altitude
questions.explanation: QRC Exercise 15, Spiral dive recovery: reduce power first, then roll wings level, then pitch up gently — power and pitch only after the wings are level to avoid tightening the spiral.

questions.prompt: Spiral dive recovery: what is the FIRST action?
choices: Pull up firmly to stop the descent
Apply full power
Reduce the power
Apply full opposite rudder
questions.explanation: QRC Exercise 15, Spiral dive recovery item 1: “Reduce the power”, then roll out gently wings level, then pitch up gently. (Full opposite rudder belongs to wing dip/spin recovery in Exercise 11.)

questions.prompt: Forced landing: what is the first speed-related action after the engine failure?
choices: Pitch for 90 KIAS and start the Mayday call
Immediately select flaps T/O and slow to 60 KIAS
Maintain altitude till speed bleeds off to 75 KIAS, then pitch for glide attitude and trim for 75 KIAS
Dive to 110 KIAS to reach a distant field
questions.explanation: QRC Exercise 16, Forced landing items 1–2: maintain altitude till speed bleeds off to 75 KIAS while looking for a field, then pitch for glide attitude and trim for 75 KIAS.

questions.prompt: Forced landing: below which altitude do you turn direct to base leg for the most suitable landing area?
choices: 500 ft
questions.explanation: QRC Exercise 16, Forced landing item 3: depending on altitude/position turn downwind; below 1200 ft turn direct base leg for the most suitable landing area.

questions.prompt: Forced landing: which emergency communication actions does the QRC list (time permitting)?
choices: PAN PAN call / transponder 7600 / ELT auto
Mayday call / transponder 7500 / landing light on
No radio call; all attention on flying only
Mayday call / transponder on 7700 / ELT Man. (T)
questions.explanation: QRC Exercise 16, Forced landing item 6: “May Day call / transponder on 7700 / ELT Man. (T) (when time permitting)”. (PAN PAN is used for the precautionary landing in Exercise 17.)

questions.prompt: On final in a forced landing, where should you initially aim in the field?
choices: At the very beginning of the field
At the last third of the field
At the 1000 ft point markers
At 1/3 of the field, to guarantee making the field
questions.explanation: QRC Exercise 16, Forced landing item 10: “On final aim at 1/3 of the field to guarantee making the field”; only when landing is assured shift the aiming point to the beginning of the field (item 14).

questions.prompt: Forced landing speeds: give the QRC values for the glide, the approach with flaps T/O, and the planned full-flaps landing speed.

parts.label: Flaps T/O when landing assured, adjust attitude for

questions.explanation: QRC Exercise 16, Forced landing items 2, 11–13: trim 75 KIAS; flaps T/O when landing assured and adjust attitude for 70 KIAS; plan full flaps landing 60 KIAS.

questions.prompt: Order the forced landing procedure from engine failure to final approach.
steps: Maintain altitude till speed bleeds off to 75 KIAS; pitch for glide attitude and trim for 75 KIAS
Turn downwind and select a landing area (below 1200 ft turn direct base leg)
Perform abbreviated troubleshoot; Mayday call / transponder 7700 / ELT Man. (T)
Proceed to the 1000 ft point; expanded troubleshoot / restart if possible
After passing the 1000 ft point, turn to base leg
On final aim at 1/3 of the field; flaps T/O when landing assured
Adjust attitude for 70 KIAS; plan full flaps landing at 60 KIAS
Perform crash drills
questions.explanation: QRC Exercise 16, Forced landing procedure items 1–13 and crash drills, in QRC order.

questions.prompt: Forced landing crash drills: which set is correct, and what does (T) mean?
choices: Seat belts fastened, fuel selector closed (T), flaps set, electric master off (T); (T) = TOUCH DRILL ONLY
Seat belts fastened, fuel selector open, flaps up, electric master on; (T) = TRAINING ONLY
Seat belts loose, fuel selector closed, flaps set, electric master off; (T) = TAXI ONLY
Seat belts fastened, fuel selector closed (T), flaps up, electric master on (T); (T) = TOUCHDOWN ONLY
questions.explanation: QRC Exercise 16, Crash drills: seat belts fastened, fuel selector closed (T), flaps set, electric master off (T); “(T) = TOUCH DRILL ONLY!!!”.

questions.prompt: When should you consider a precautionary landing, and what are the QRC requirements for a landing field?
questions.model_answer: Consider a precautionary landing when: weather deteriorates below VMC minima; after UDP; or other circumstances affecting flight safety that require it (the aircraft should be technically in good condition). Field requirements: no obstacles on final (or upwind); long enough (minimum 300 m); headwind (or light crosswind); flat; preference for (short) grassland over plowed land.
questions.explanation: QRC Exercise 17, “Consider a precautionary landing when” and “Requirements for a landing field” lists.

questions.prompt: Precautionary landing: which radio/transponder/ELT actions does the QRC prescribe?
choices: Mayday call / transponder 7700 / ELT Man. (T)
PAN PAN call / transponder on 7700 / ELT Man. (T)
PAN PAN call / transponder 7600 / ELT off
No call required, squawk 7000
questions.explanation: QRC Exercise 17, procedure item 3: “PAN PAN call / transponder on 7700 / ELT man (T)”. (Mayday belongs to the forced landing, Exercise 16.)

questions.prompt: Precautionary landing: give the QRC circuit height, inspection run height, and minimum field length.
questions.explanation: QRC Exercise 17: fly a close circuit at 500 ft AGL (item 5), inspection run at 200 ft AGL (item 7), field long enough min. 300 m (field requirements).

questions.prompt: In the precautionary landing pattern, when do you turn to final?
choices: When the landing area is 45° behind
When the landing area is 90° abeam
When the landing area is 60° behind the wing
Immediately after the inspection run at 200 ft AGL
questions.explanation: QRC Exercise 17, procedure item 14: “Turn to final when the landing area is 60° behind the wing”. (45° behind is the base-turn cue in the normal circuit, Exercise 13.)

questions.prompt: Order the precautionary landing procedure after selecting the field.
steps: Perform downwind checks, select flaps T/O, PAN PAN call / transponder 7700 / ELT man (T)
Position on downwind of the suitable field and fly a close circuit at 500 ft AGL
Make a descending turn towards the area and carry out an inspection run at 200 ft AGL
Climb back to 500 ft AGL, flaps up on the up-wind leg, turn crosswind then downwind (downwind checks)
Turn to final when the landing area is 60° behind the wing
Carry out a short field landing
Evacuate the airplane and call RAC
questions.explanation: QRC Exercise 17, Precautionary landing procedure items 1–16 condensed in QRC order.

questions.prompt: Soft field landing (grass runway): what does the QRC prescribe after touchdown?
choices: Brake firmly and bring the aircraft to a stop as soon as possible
Lower the nose immediately and vacate the runway at the first exit
Maintain backpressure on the elevator to relieve the nose wheel, decelerate gently without excessive brakes, keep the aircraft rolling, and perform the after landing checks while rolling
Hold the nose wheel off as long as possible, then stop on the runway to perform the after landing checks
questions.explanation: QRC Exercise 13, Soft field landing: after touchdown and during taxi maintain backpressure on the elevator to relieve the nose wheel, decelerate gently without excessive brakes, keep aileron in the wind, keep the aircraft rolling, and perform the after landing checks while rolling.
